lines: Riley Chen
+1 (555) 010-7731 | riley.chen@example.com | example.com/in/riley-chen
EDUCATION
Northfield School of Management | MBA | Metro City, USA | Sep 2023 - Jun 2025
Lakeview University | B.A. in Economics | Lake City, USA | Sep 2014 - Jun 2018
EXPERIENCE
Coastal Marine Services | Diesel Mechanic | Lake City, USA | Jul 2025 - Present
- Rebuilt diesel engines and gearboxes for a fleet of 14 commercial fishing vessels, keeping dry-dock time under 5 days per job.
- Maintained hydraulic winch systems and logged service records for the harbor authority's annual inspections.
Crestline Logistics | Operations Analyst | Lake City, USA | Jul 2018 - Aug 2023
- Owned the weekly carrier scorecards for the regional managers and the monthly review meeting that discussed them.
- Cut warehouse pick errors 30% at two sites by redesigning slotting rules with the floor supervisors and retraining 45 pickers on the new layout.
- Ran the quarterly S&OP review across sales, finance and operations for 12 consecutive quarters, introducing a consensus forecast that cut forecast error from 18% to 11%.

- Led the rollout of a route-planning tool to 3 depots while rewriting the standard operating procedures, running driver training and taking over vendor negotiations for the telematics contract, which saved 1,800 driver hours a year across the region.
Harbor Payments | Associate Product Manager Intern | Metro City, USA | Jun 2024 - Aug 2024
- Redesigned merchant onboarding around a single verification step, cutting median time to first payment from 9 days to 4 across 2,300 new merchants in the pilot region.
- Lifted checkout conversion from 61% to 66% by testing a one-page flow against the three-step flow across 40,000 sessions, then shipping it to all merchants.
- Prioritized the dispute roadmap with RICE, scoring Reach as the number of support tickets each feature would close.
- After interviewing 25 merchants, mapping chargeback reasons, sizing the loss by segment and drafting a business case with finance, set the next quarter's roadmap priority.
- Ran the checkout A/B test with randomization by session and reported the 5-point conversion lift as the effect on merchants' customers.
- Presented the onboarding results and a follow-up roadmap to the payments leadership team, who funded the rollout to two more regions.
PROJECTS
Campus Food Rescue App | Product Lead | Student Venture | Oct 2023 - Present
- Launched a surplus-food pickup app to 3,100 students with two dining halls, redistributing 9 tonnes of food that would have been thrown away in its first year.
- Raised weekly active users from 400 to 1,150, a 150% increase, by adding pickup reminders chosen after 60 user interviews.
- Raised the pickup-slot fill rate by 20% across two dining halls, from 75% to 95%, by setting up a volunteer shift system.
MBA Consulting Practicum | Team Lead | Regional Hospital Network | Jan 2024 - May 2024
- Sized a $2.4M annual saving from consolidating outpatient scheduling across 4 clinics; the client funded a pilot based on the model.
- Patient intake at 4 clinics was mapped and the intake form was shortened, with the changes adopted by front-desk staff.
- Presented the final recommendation to the hospital COO and clinic directors, who approved a 90-day scheduling pilot at two clinics.
SKILLS
Product: roadmapping, A/B testing, user interviews, requirements writing
Tools: Jira, Amplitude, Excel

items.says: The résumé could be more clearly targeted to product roles.
items.because: Product work should stand out more.

items.says: Consider adding a relevant concentration or product activity.
items.because: It could help explain the transition to product roles.

items.says: Be ready to explain the move from an MBA and product internship to a mechanic role.
items.because: The transition may prompt questions.

items.says: Clarify how many engines or jobs you personally completed.
items.because: A fleet of 14 does not show the scale of your work.

items.says: Specify whether dry-dock time was consistently under five days or averaged under five days.
Add the scope or an outcome of the hydraulic-systems work.
items.because: The line lists duties without showing their effect.

items.says: Move Crestline below the 2024 internship.
items.because: Experience should be in reverse chronological order.

items.says: Identify a decision or improvement the scorecards supported.
items.because: Owning a report and meeting says less about your impact than what managers did with them.

items.says: Clarify the measurement period or comparison for the 30% reduction.
items.because: It would make the figure credible.

items.says: State how forecast error was measured.
items.because: The measure may not be obvious in your target industry.

items.says: Narrow the line to the contributions that produced the 1,800-hour saving.
items.because: Combining rollout, SOPs, training, negotiations, and savings makes the causal link hard to follow.

items.says: Clarify whether the saved hours were measured or estimated.
Place the internship between Coastal Marine Services and Crestline Logistics and give its strongest bullets prominence.
items.because: It is the most relevant experience for product applications.

items.says: Clarify whether all 2,300 merchants were exposed to the new flow.
Clarify whether the time-to-first-payment comparison used comparable cohorts.
Check whether the conversion rates are session-based.
items.because: The population should be stated precisely.

items.says: Check whether the rollout covered all merchants.
items.because: The rollout scope should be stated precisely.

items.says: Reach is incorrectly defined as the number of support tickets a feature would close.
items.because: Reach should represent people or accounts affected over a defined period.

items.says: Explain the support-ticket proxy if that is what you used.
items.because: Tickets a feature might eliminate can be a useful input.

items.says: Distinguish this roadmap decision from the preceding prioritization bullet or consolidate them.
items.because: The bullets overlap, and the long sequence of activities hides the result.

items.says: The reported lift implies a measured effect on merchants or individual customers.
items.because: The test was randomized and measured at the session level.

items.says: Remove or distinguish the A/B-test methodology bullet unless its design matters to the target roles.
items.because: It overlaps with the checkout-conversion bullet.

items.says: Clarify whether the two-region rollout was funded, launched, or completed.
items.because: Those are different claims.

items.says: Confirm that “Present” reflects ongoing work and make your continuing involvement clear.
items.because: The project extends beyond your June 2025 graduation.

items.says: Clarify whether 3,100 students means eligible students, sign-ups, or users.
Substantiate that all nine tonnes would otherwise have been discarded, or describe it simply as food redistributed.
The increase from 400 to 1,150 is 187.5%, not 150%.
Check the comparison periods for weekly active users.
Check whether reminders can reasonably be credited for the full increase.
The change from 75% to 95% is 20 percentage points, not a 20% relative increase.
Specify the comparison period for the fill-rate change if available.
Replace the passive description with your contribution.
Include an observed result from the shorter form if you have one.
items.because: Otherwise, do not imply a measured improvement.

items.says: The pilot approval substantially duplicates the first practicum bullet.
items.because: The first bullet already says the client funded a pilot.

items.says: Make sure you can substantiate the requirements-writing skill.
items.because: The review points to testing and interview examples but not requirements-writing work.
